value.rationale: The squared self-ambiguity is the intrinsic point-spread probability law for continuous analytic wavelet analysis. The theorem classifies all time-displacement moments for every real analytic Cauchy order, identifies the sharp q=2a+1 boundary where localization penalties cease to be defined, supplies the explicit tail constant, and explains the geometric mechanism through a total-variation conditional limit of dilation given extreme time displacement. This is a natural complete family-level invariant and sharp time-scale coupling law, not a chosen finite example or generic restatement of a kernel coefficient. It can benchmark moment-based wavelet design and tail-sensitive localization.
